newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana bourse falls on bank lending scandal.
newsitem.headline: Ghana bourse falls on bank lending scandal.

text.p: The Ghana Stock Exchange All-Share Index slumped on Wednesday, dragged down by Ghana Commercial Bank and a scandal over unauthorised lending, brokers said.

The Index fell 4.37 points from 354.04 points to 349.67 points. Ghana Commercial Bank shed 40 cedis to close at 600 cedis after the finance ministry announced this week that its managing director Helen Lokko had been retired over the scandal involving 70 billion cedis of unauthorised lending to a supermarket chain.
Bids outpaced offers for the third time this year at 2,344,260 to 938,620, with 46,220 shares changing hands.

The other loser was Mechanical Lloyd Co (-1 cedi to 53 cedis). Ashanti Goldfields Co (+5 TO 20,820), Kumasi Brewery Ltd (+14 TO 700) and Metalloplastic Ltd (+8 to 160) Pioneer Tobacco Co (+1 to 137) were the risers.

In March, last year Ghana Commercial Bank went public and sold 42 percent of its shares, while the sale of only 30 percent had been initially envisaged. In November, the Denko Industrial Corp Berhad of Malaysia acquired 40 percent of the bank. The Malaysians are expected to take over management as soon as the deal is ratified by president Jerry Rawlings.
